name: Singapore
tagline: Everything in English — and a subsidy that comes with a three-year contract
summary: Singapore is the easiest Asian system for a Danish IB student to understand, because everything already runs in English and the qualifications are read directly. It is also the one place on this site where the headline price is not the price. The government offers international students the MOE Tuition Grant, which roughly halves the fee — and in exchange you sign an agreement, guaranteed by two named sureties, contractually obliging you to work for a Singapore entity for three years after you graduate. That is not a formality and it is not a suggestion. It is a contract, and you choose it by ticking a box on the application form months before anyone explains it. Underneath that sit three quite different Singapores: six Autonomous Universities that share an August intake and a joint acceptance portal, two arts institutions whose deadline falls the previous November, and a set of private institutions and foreign branch campuses that award somebody else's degree.
whyConsider: Every degree is taught in English, and NUS and NTU are consistently ranked among the strongest universities in Asia.

The MOE Tuition Grant cuts NTU's international fee from roughly SGD 36,350–40,600 a year to roughly SGD 21,400–21,800 — about SGD 60,000–75,000 across a four-year degree — if you accept the service obligation.

Singapore has thought about the July problem and says what it does. NTU takes your application on predicted grades in March and wants the real results within three days of release; NUS tells May-session IB candidates they will hear by the third week of July. Very few systems are this explicit.

The three-year service obligation, read the other way round, is a guaranteed graduate pathway into one of Asia's strongest job markets — and Singapore actively wants the people it has subsidised to stay.
Offers are accepted once, through a shared Joint Acceptance Portal across the six Autonomous Universities, rather than replied to one by one.
SUTD, built with MIT, runs a genuinely unusual design-led curriculum with a common first year and no departments.
watchOuts: The Tuition Grant service obligation is a contract and should be read as one. NTU states that a non-Singaporean taking the grant signs an agreement contractually obliging them to work in a Singapore entity for three years after graduating. MOE adds that only full-time employment after graduation counts, that a job search typically takes about six months, and that deferring the bond for postgraduate study needs approval at least eight weeks ahead. It is a decision about where you live into the 2030s.

You do not sign it alone. Two sureties of any nationality, over 21 and under 65, not undischarged bankrupts, with the financial means to cover the liability — MOE encourages immediate family — sign alongside you and are jointly liable for liquidated damages if the bond is not served.

The exposure is not only at the end. MOE states that a student who withdraws from the course midway is liable, with their sureties, for liquidated damages on the whole grant received plus 10% compounded interest a year, with late-payment interest on top. Illness, homesickness or a change of mind in second year all fall inside that.

You elect the grant on the application form, confirm it at offer stage in July, and sign it in September or October once you are already in Singapore. By then you have flown, paid and moved in. Treat the tick-box as the decision point, not the signature.

The deadlines are not shared and are months apart. LASALLE asks you to apply by 1 November 2026, NUS closes 17 February 2027, NTU closes 19 March 2027 — and SUTD, SIT, SMU, SUSS and NAFA have published nothing for 2027 at all.

NTU will not consider a May-session IB candidate for Medicine, the Renaissance Engineering Programme, or Arts and Science (Academic Discipline & Education), because those decide before your results exist.

Actual results are due at NTU within three days of release — the first week of July, in the middle of the Danish summer. The IBO transcript authorisation that makes that possible must be arranged before July, and an application without it gets no outcome at all.

Whether an international student at LASALLE or NAFA can take the Tuition Grant, and would therefore be bonded, is not established. The University of the Arts Singapore names only Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents and refers the question back to the colleges.
Only NTU's fee table could be read. NUS, SMU and SUTD figures are left blank on purpose.
Denmark's SU works differently for a full degree outside the EU/EEA. Check su.dk early.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: No national minimum and no published institutional one we could verify. Singapore's universities publish indicative grade profiles for the Singapore-Cambridge A-level rather than for the IB. Competitive applicants to NUS and NTU are generally said to be in the high 30s to low 40s; that figure is unverified and is recorded here as a caution rather than a threshold. Ask admissions for the published profile.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Programme-specific Higher Level requirements apply — engineering and computing normally want HL Mathematics, medicine HL Chemistry and Biology — and were not verified programme by programme in this pass. The rule that was verified is a different kind: NTU excludes a May-session IB candidate from Medicine, Renaissance Engineering, and Arts and Science (Academic Discipline & Education) entirely, because those programmes decide before IB results exist. That is a subject restriction imposed by the calendar rather than by the syllabus, and it is the one most likely to catch a Danish applicant.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: No conversion table. IB points are read directly against a programme's profile. NUS goes further than most and treats the IB Diploma as its own applicant group with its own application window, separate from other international qualifications.
notes: Predicted grades carry the initial assessment and offers are conditional on the final diploma. NTU requires actual results within three days of their release in July 2027 and requires direct access to the official transcript through the IB organisation before July 2027.
NUS tells IB applicants sitting the May 2027 session that they will hear by the third week of July 2027, where most of its applicants hear in May.
IB English A or B is normally accepted as proof of English. Confirm with each university.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: All of them. English is the medium of instruction across the entire Singapore higher education system.
language.englishProof: IB English A or B is normally accepted; some universities may still ask for IELTS or TOEFL. Not verified institution by institution.
notes: Singapore has four official languages and the universities operate entirely in English.
You will hear Singlish everywhere and pick it up whether you want to or not. It is not a barrier.

feeContext.summary: Singapore does not recognise EU or EEA status. Its categories are Singapore Citizen, Singapore Permanent Resident and International Student, and a Danish student is the third. See the non-EU row.

At NTU, for a student accepted in 2026 and with the rate fixed at the year-of-entry level for the whole degree: roughly SGD 21,400–21,800 a year with the MOE Tuition Grant, and SGD 36,350 (non-laboratory) to SGD 40,600 (laboratory-based) without it, inclusive of 9% GST. Medicine is non-subsidised only at SGD 91,250 a year for non-ASEAN internationals, and the Renaissance Engineering Programme non-subsidised at SGD 32,000. NUS, SMU and SUTD figures could not be read and none of NTU's may be carried to them.
feeContext.priceYear: AY2026/27, fixed for the degree duration

sectorLandscape.summary: Singapore's post-secondary system divides three ways, and the division decides the calendar, the money and the degree. Six Autonomous Universities — NUS, NTU, SMU, SUTD, SIT and SUSS, named as a group by the universities themselves — are publicly funded, carry the MOE Tuition Grant and settle their offers through one shared Joint Acceptance Portal. The two arts institutions, LASALLE and NAFA, now award their degrees through the University of the Arts Singapore and admit on portfolio and audition months earlier. Everything else is a registered Private Education Institution, including the Australian, American and French branch campuses, which award the parent's degree on a trimester calendar. Below all of this sits the route nobody mentions to foreigners: the five polytechnics and the Institute of Technical Education, which are where most Singaporeans actually go.

routes.what: NUS, NTU, SMU, SUTD, SIT and SUSS. Government-funded, degree-awarding in their own right, and the only institutions where the MOE Tuition Grant and its three-year service obligation apply to an international student. You apply to each separately — six forms, six fees, six deadlines from November to March — and then accept one offer through a single Joint Acceptance Portal that lists all of them.
routes.note: The group is not a ranking. SIT is an applied university whose intake is overwhelmingly domestic polytechnic graduates, SUSS is built around part-time and flexible study, and SUTD is tiny and design-led. Only NUS, NTU and SMU are what a European would picture.

routes.what: LASALLE College of the Arts and the Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts, allied since 2024 into the University of the Arts Singapore, which now validates, confers and awards their degrees — LASALLE's were previously awarded by Goldsmiths, University of London. Entry is on portfolio and audition, with one intake each August and a deadline that falls the previous November, months ahead of the universities.
routes.note: Whether an international student here can take the MOE Tuition Grant is not established. UAS names Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents as eligible and says nothing about anyone else.

routes.englishName: private institution or foreign branch campus
routes.what: Registered private providers, including the branch campuses — James Cook University Singapore, Curtin Singapore, DigiPen Singapore, ESSEC Asia-Pacific — and SIM Global Education, which delivers partner universities' degrees without awarding its own. The degree is Australian, American, British or French rather than Singaporean, the structure is usually trimesters with several intakes a year, and the MOE Tuition Grant does not reach here.
routes.note: Singapore registers these institutions for a fixed term rather than chartering them, and the registration number and expiry date are published on their own pages. A registration expiring inside the length of your degree is a fair question to ask.

routes.what: Five polytechnics — Singapore, Ngee Ann, Temasek, Nanyang and Republic — awarding three-year applied diplomas that are the ordinary post-secondary destination for a large share of Singaporeans, and a recognised route onward into the Autonomous Universities with advanced standing. This is Singapore's answer to the Danish erhvervsakademi and it is almost never described to a foreign applicant.
routes.note: Not researched here. Whether an IB Diploma holder from abroad can enrol, what it costs and whether the Tuition Grant applies are all open questions. Recorded because the route exists, is large, and explains why SIT's admissions calendar is built around polytechnic results rather than IB ones.

routes.what: The ITE, awarding Nitec and Higher Nitec vocational qualifications below diploma level, feeding into the polytechnics and into work. It appears in this record only because LASALLE's Early Admission Exercise names final-year Nitec and Higher Nitec students alongside IB Year 4 students, which is the kind of detail that shows where the system's ladders actually are.
routes.note: Not researched. Named so that the route is visible rather than invisible.

jurisdictions.name: The six Autonomous Universities
jurisdictions.summary: NUS, NTU, SMU, SUTD, SIT and SUSS — the group NUS names in its own words. Publicly funded, degree-awarding, one August intake, and the only place an international student meets the MOE Tuition Grant and its three-year bond. Six separate applications, one shared acceptance.

variations.label: Deadlines
variations.summary: NUS's IB Diploma window runs 16 December 2026 to 17 February 2027; NTU's runs 15 October 2026 to 19 March 2027 with documents by 22 March. SUTD and SIT publish their 2026 cycle only. SMU's and SUSS's pages could not be read. Actual IB results are due at NTU within three days of release in July 2027.

variations.label: Cost and the Tuition Grant
variations.summary: Roughly SGD 21,400–21,800 a year at NTU with the grant against SGD 36,350–40,600 without, fixed at the year-of-entry rate. The grant is elected on the application form and paid for with a contractual obligation to work in a Singapore entity for three years after graduation, signed with two jointly liable sureties.

jurisdictions.name: The arts institutions
jurisdictions.summary: LASALLE College of the Arts and the Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts, whose degrees are now validated, conferred and awarded by the University of the Arts Singapore. Portfolio and audition entry, one August intake, and a calendar that runs months ahead of the universities.

variations.label: Deadlines
variations.summary: LASALLE opens on 1 October 2026 and asks you to apply by 1 November 2026 for an August 2027 start, with outcomes by 23 December 2026 — before NUS has even opened. Music closes 28 February 2027. NAFA has published nothing for 2027.

variations.label: The Tuition Grant
variations.summary: Not established for an international student. The University of the Arts Singapore names Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents as eligible for the Tuition Grant on selected bachelor's programmes, says nothing about anyone else, and refers the question back to LASALLE and NAFA. Ask before assuming either way — the answer determines whether you would be bonded.

jurisdictions.name: Private institutions and foreign branch campuses
jurisdictions.summary: James Cook University Singapore, Curtin Singapore, DigiPen Singapore, ESSEC Asia-Pacific and SIM Global Education. Registered Private Education Institutions awarding an Australian, American, French or British degree rather than a Singaporean one, usually on trimesters with several intakes a year, and outside the MOE Tuition Grant.

variations.label: Deadlines
variations.summary: None published for 2027 by any of the five on the pages consulted. The trimester structure means several starts a year rather than one August cliff, which softens the consequence — but that is a fact about the structure, not a date.

variations.label: Cost
variations.summary: Not established, and the MOE Tuition Grant is not expected to apply because none of these is an Autonomous University — which also means no bond, no sureties and no service obligation. Confirm both with the institution.

notes: Grouping decision. institutionGrouping is "jurisdiction" with three jurisdictions each of kind "sector". The division is not a convenience: whether an institution is an Autonomous University decides whether the MOE Tuition Grant and its three-year bond exist for you at all, whether you accept through the Joint Acceptance Portal, and whether your deadline falls in March or the previous November. Grouping by city would have been meaningless in a country that is one city. The "sector" grouping was considered and rejected because it carries no Application Route, and each of these three divisions has a different one.
The single most urgent item in this record is LASALLE: its window for August 2027 opens on 1 October 2026 and closes on 1 November 2026, eight days and five weeks after this record was written.

Three dates on the autonomous-university route are derived rather than published and are marked provisional: NTU's actual-results deadline of 9 July 2027 is 6 July plus three days; the IBO transcript authorisation of 30 June 2027 is the last day satisfying NTU's "before July 2027"; and NUS's outcome date of 21 July 2027 is a reading of "the third week of July". Each carries a note saying so.

Not established: SMU's and SUSS's 2027 dates, because their admissions pages sit behind a bot-detection service and one asks for a CAPTCHA, which this project does not complete — that is our gap, not theirs, and ev-sg-smu-unreadable records it; SUTD's and SIT's and NAFA's 2027 dates, which those institutions have not yet published; tuition at NUS, SMU and SUTD; indicative IB grade profiles anywhere; whether the Tuition Grant reaches an international student at LASALLE, NAFA or any private institution; and what the polytechnic route offers an IB holder from abroad.
Programme-level records not yet created. Stages 1–5 of the research brief are done for this Destination; stage 6 is not.
